# Kyoto 3-Day Relaxed Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A calm spring itinerary with easy transit, 3-star-or-better stays, and one vegetarian-friendly dinner each night. Costs below are estimated for **2 adults** and keep the pace to **2 major activities max per day**.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

## Day 1 — April 10: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and settle near **Kyoto Station** or **Shijo/Kawaramachi** for simple subway and bus access.
- **Afternoon:** Easy first outing to **Kiyomizu-dera** and the nearby lanes of **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka**.
- **Dinner:** Vegetarian-friendly kaiseki or tofu-focused dinner in central Kyoto.
- **Major activities:** 2
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170–$260, meals $80–$120, local transit $10–$20, snacks/entry $20–$35, **day total $280–$435**

## Day 2 — April 11: Arashiyama and Temple Gardens
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and riverside area before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one calm second stop: **Tenryu-ji** gardens or a slow walk by the Katsura River.
- **Dinner:** Vegetarian-friendly dinner around **Shijo** or back near the hotel for convenience.
- **Major activities:** 2
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170–$260, meals $80–$120, local transit $12–$22, entry/tea $20–$40, **day total $282–$442**

## Day 3 — April 12: Northern Kyoto or Fushimi Sake District
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** for a classic Kyoto highlight, or swap to **Fushimi Inari** if you want a more active but still flexible final morning.
- **Afternoon:** Keep it light with a café break, souvenir shopping, or a short canal-side stroll in **Fushimi**.
- **Dinner:** Final vegetarian-friendly dinner near Kyoto Station before departure or a relaxed neighborhood restaurant.
- **Major activities:** 2
- **Estimated cost:** Hotel $170–$260, meals $80–$120, local transit $10–$20, entry/shopping $25–$50, **day total $285–$450**

# Recommended Stay Areas and Hotel Options

## Best 3-Star-or-Better Hotel Zones
- **Kyoto Station area:** easiest for trains, luggage, and day trips
- **Shijo/Kawaramachi:** best for dining, shopping, and central bus/subway access
- **Gion/Higashiyama edge:** best atmosphere, but usually pricier and less convenient for rail

## Ranked Hotel Shortlist
Option 1: **The Royal Park Hotel Kyoto Sanjo** | Central, walkable, and strong transit access | Great for Shijo/Kawaramachi base
Action: [Button: View Hotel](https://www.royalparkhotels.co.jp/the/kyotosanjo/en/)

Option 2: **Hotel Granvia Kyoto** | Directly connected to Kyoto Station | Best for convenience and luggage ease
Action: [Button: View Hotel](https://www.granvia-kyoto.co.jp/en/)

Option 3: **Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Station** | Reliable 3-star-plus comfort near transit | Good value for easy arrivals/departures
Action: [Button: View Hotel](https://www.gardenhotels.co.jp/kyoto-station/eng/)

Option 4: **Hotel Resol Kyoto Kawaramachi Sanjo** | Central, compact, and well-located for dining | Strong walkability for a relaxed trip
Action: [Button: View Hotel](https://www.resol-hotel.jp/kyoto-kawaramachi/en/)

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults
- **Hotel target per night:** $170–$260
- **3-night lodging total:** **$510–$780**
- **Meals total:** **$240–$360**
- **Transit + entries + snacks:** **$100–$190**
- **Estimated trip total excluding flights:** **$850–$1,330**

This keeps you comfortably under the **$1,800** cap, leaving room for nicer dinners, taxis after long days, or upgraded rooms.

# Packing Checklist for Kyoto in Mid-April

## Clothing
- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- 3 days of easy-to-layer outfits
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Socks you can wear all day for temple visits

## Travel Essentials
- Passport and digital copies
- Credit/debit cards plus some yen cash
- Phone charger and power bank
- Universal adapter if needed
- IC card option on phone or physical transit card

## Spring-Specific Extras
- Allergy meds if pollen affects you
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Small foldable tote for shopping and snacks
- Tissue pack and hand sanitizer
- Reusable water bottle

## Temple and Transit Tips
- Clothing that is modest enough for temple visits
- Easy slip-on shoes if you expect frequent indoor/outdoor stops
- A small day bag rather than a large backpack for crowded areas
